newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: New U.S. ambassador arrives in Nicaragua.
newsitem.headline: New U.S. ambassador arrives in Nicaragua.

text.p: The new U.S. ambassador to Nicaragua, Lino Gutierrez, arrived in the capital Managua on Tuesday and said he was ready to work with the new right-wing government that will take power on Jan. 10.
"Personally, I'm ready to work closely with President-elect Arnoldo Aleman and the leaders of the new government in their task of carrying Nicaragua into the 21st century," he told a news conference.
Gutierrez, 45, a Cuban-born career diplomat, begins a three-year term in Nicaragua and replaces outgoing Ambassador John Maisto, who likely will head to an ambassadorial post in Venezuela.
Gutierrez headed the Nicaragua desk at the State Department in 1981 during the left-wing Sandinista government.

He said his government will continue supporting Nicaragua's return to a free-market economy and democracy, a process begun in 1990 when Violeta Chamorro, at the head of a broad centrist coalition, toppled former Sandinista President Daniel Ortega at the ballot box.
Gutierrez said Nicaragua's Oct. 20 elections won by Aleman were free and fair and had renovated "the faith in democracy."
"I feel fortunate to have arrived at a moment of such hope for Nicaragua," he said.

Among the concerns of the U.S. government will be human rights, drug trafficking, the smuggling of illegal aliens, sustainable economic growth and a "quick and just" resolution of the remaining complaints by U.S. citizens whose property was confiscated during the 1979-1990 Sandinista government, he said.
He said it still had not been decided if President Bill Clinton would attend Aleman's Jan. 10 inauguration.
